userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need my prompt to name the real PreToolUse allowlist and describe the reviewer as a Task-in-context worker whose summary the sidecar pushes, so I do not attempt spawns that will be denied or expect a self-pushing 3rd-pane TUI reviewer that does not exist.
acceptanceCriteria: In both prompt copies, the Identity/allowlist reference lists the full set enforced by orch-agent-allowlist.sh: Explore, Plan, claude-code-guide, subagent-planner, subagent-auditor, subagent-reviewer (not the subset 'subagent-planner, subagent-auditor'). [oracle: for f in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md; do grep -q 'claude-code-guide' "$f" && grep -q 'subagent-reviewer' "$f" && grep -q 'subagent-auditor' "$f" || exit 1; done]

In both prompt copies the reviewer is described as a Task-in-context worker spawned under the PreToolUse allowlist whose one-line summary is pushed by the sidecar (worker-report), NOT as a 3rd-pane interactive TUI worker that self-pushes via send-keys. [oracle: for f in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md; do grep -q 'worker-report' "$f" || exit 1; done]
The reviewer/worker wording no longer claims workers self-send their summary line to the orchestrator pane (the sidecar is the single pusher). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

userStories.title: Truth-up dispatch protocol + sidecar loop + issueNumber
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need the dispatch protocol to reflect that plan/next/ship write a signal file (only review/issue inject a slash via send-keys), that cam next is one-shot (the sidecar loops), and that issueNumber is consumed at ship, so I stop looping /cam-next on a nonexistent sentinel and stop mis-describing how commands execute.
acceptanceCriteria: Neither prompt copy references the CAM_LOOP_STATUS=COMPLETE sentinel, and the conversation-contract 'implementa/go' row no longer instructs looping /cam-next until that sentinel. [oracle: for f in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md; do grep -q 'CAM_LOOP_STATUS=COMPLETE' "$f" && exit 1; done; true]

In both copies the dispatch protocol states that plan/next/ship write a signal to .claude/cam-loop.local.md (deterministic runners then execute) and that only review/issue inject a slash command into the pane via send-keys. [oracle: for f in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md; do grep -q 'cam-loop.local.md' "$f" || exit 1; done]

Both copies no longer claim /cam-plan and /cam-ship run in the orchestrator's context and return a result line; they are described as writing a signal that a deterministic runner executes. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Both copies describe issueNumber accurately: it is consumed at ship time, not a supervisor gate (the pre-flight anchor-to-issue guidance may stay, but it must not claim the supervisor gates on issueNumber). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]

userStories.title: Truth-up handoff required fields + close-on-ship
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need the self-handoff section to state the real required fields and HANDOFF_DUE trigger, and the issue-system section to state that ship auto-closes the issue (manual close being a fallback only), so I do not over-declare handoff requirements or double-close issues at ship.
acceptanceCriteria: In both copies the self-handoff section states that only schemaVersion, writtenAt, and reason are required fields (matching handoff schema), documents projectContext as an optional field, and states HANDOFF_DUE is armed only by `cam journal append --cycle-close` (not by every successful append). [oracle: for f in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md; do grep -q 'projectContext' "$f" && grep -q -- '--cycle-close' "$f" || exit 1; done]

In both copies the close-on-ship text states ship auto-closes the issue (ship-pr.ts) and that orchestrator manual close is a documented fallback only (used when the sidecar auto-close was skipped, e.g. a stale binary); the unconditional close-on-ship instruction is removed to prevent double-close. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
